context: Standing operator confirmation (every found bug: register and fix, never ask); found by the main thread on push CI run 41486371753 (feature/0.8.2 6cd90f9): UnicodeDecodeError on all 4 windows-latest rows. Path.read_text() without an encoding decodes with the locale codec (cp1252 on Windows); auto_tag_publish_master.yml, pr_to_development.yml, pr_to_master.yml and test_on_push.yml hold UTF-8 emoji bytes (0x9d, 0x8f) cp1252 cannot decode. Reproduced on Linux with python -X warn_default_encoding -W error::EncodingWarning. cause: The shim's save wrapper read every save destination back with read_artifact, whose csv fallback cannot read a sqlite database, so the read raised inside the agent's script.
context: provenance's docstring promises None when every artifact column equals a column the script generated through rand_engine on a re-run; the shim's save wrapper reads back every save destination with read_artifact, whose csv fallback cannot read a sqlite database, so the read raises inside the agent's script
expected: None: the shim records the sqlite save and leaves the script's outcome unchanged; out.csv passes against its get_df frame
repro: PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<repo>/evals python -c "import _check, sys; print(_check.provenance('work', 'work/s.py', ['out.csv'], python=sys.executable))" where work/s.py saves DataGenerator(spec, seed=1).size(10) with .write.format('sqlite').option('table', 't').save('out.sqlite') and writes the same generator's get_df() to out.csv
solution: The read-back runs only when the writer wrote files (write_format is not sqlite), the same test save itself makes.
symptom: a script that saves a sqlite table and writes out.csv from get_df returns 'provenance: the script exited 1 on re-run: ... UnicodeDecodeError: utf-8 codec can't decode byte 0x89 in position 99' instead of None
title: The provenance re-run crashes the agent's script when it saves to sqlite

cause: The writer passed indent to DataFrame.to_json(lines=True), which spreads a record over several lines, so an accepted option contradicted the one-record-per-line contract.
context: docs/3_WRITING_FILES.md:32 states json is written by pandas with orient records, one record per line; :40 lists indent among the accepted json options, and specs/memory/product/output/writers-and-streaming.md:41 records it. _JsonFile (file_handler.py:211,275) and FileHandler.to_json (:396-397) pass indent to DataFrame.to_json(lines=True), which then pretty-prints each record over several lines. Found by the hotfix review of eval-shim-sqlite-save-crashes-rerun (verdict 2026-11-07T171028Z): the eval shim's save read-back of such a file kills the re-run with JSONDecodeError. master documents the same option (indent=2, pretty-print JSON).
expected: every json file the writer writes holds one record per line (docs/3_WRITING_FILES.md:32), so a JSON-lines reader reads it back
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c "from rand_engine import DataGenerator; import pandas as pd; DataGenerator({'a': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 0, 'max': 9}}}, seed=1).size(3).write.format('json').option('indent', 2).save('x.json'); pd.read_json('x.json', lines=True)" raises ValueError: Expected object or value
solution: indent leaves both json accepted-option lists and the docs table; json refuses it like any undocumented option (operator: Drop indent).
symptom: a json save with option('indent', 2) writes records spread over several lines with blank lines between them, and pd.read_json(path, lines=True) raises ValueError: Expected object or value
title: A json save with the documented indent option writes each record over several lines, which no JSON-lines reader can read

cause: read_artifact concatenated a parts directory in name order while rand_engine writers name parts randomly, so two reads of the same seeded parts differed and the order-sensitive value_hash with them
context: read_artifact (evals/_check.py, the directory branch) concatenates a directory's parts sorted by name, and value_hash is order-sensitive. The batch writer names parts part_<uuid>.csv, random on every run, so the agent's run and the re-run concatenate the same seeded parts in different orders. Found by the rc-4 Job 4 review (verdict 2026-11-07T184817Z, INFO) and reproduced on feature/0.8.2 d0488c4: 2 of 6 provenance runs passed.
expected: provenance gives the same answer on every re-run of a seeded script, and a parts directory rand_engine wrote passes (evals/_check.py provenance docstring: None when every artifact column equals a column the script generated through rand_engine on a re-run)
repro: solve.py: DataGenerator({'age': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 0, 'max': 99}}}, seed=1).size(40).write.format('csv').option('numFiles', 2).save('out'); run it once in a work dir, then call _check.provenance(work, work/solve.py, ['out'], python=sys.executable) six times with PYTHONPATH=.:evals: some calls return None, the others the matches-no-frame line
solution: read_artifact sorts a directory's parts by their content as read, so the frame no longer depends on part names
symptom: a seeded save with option('numFiles', 2), graded as its directory, returns provenance: column 'age' of out matches no frame rand_engine generated on some runs and None on others
title: provenance passes or fails at random on a multi-part save directory: the parts' random names set the concatenation order the column hash depends on

cause: provenance re-ran the script in the scratch copy before it read the delivered artifacts (rc-3 J4.T2 put the read loop after the re-run), so a script writing its artifact by absolute path rewrote the original and was graded against its own re-run, and a symlink-loop artifact crashed the copy with shutil.Error
context: evals/_check.py provenance copies workdir to a scratch dir without the artifacts, re-runs the script there, and only then reads the delivered artifacts from workdir. A script that writes by an absolute path (or through a link back into workdir) writes into workdir during the re-run, so provenance compares the re-run's output with the re-run's own record. The same read order lets a symlink loop on an artifact path crash the copy (shutil.Error on feature/0.8.2) instead of failing as not delivered. Found by the rc-4 Job 4 review r2 (verdict 2026-11-07T193238Z, MEDIUM bug proposal) and reproduced by the main thread on feature/0.8.2 fa397e2.
expected: provenance reads the delivered artifacts as delivered and never modifies them (evals/_check.py:149 'The re-run happens in a scratch copy of `workdir` without the artifacts, so the originals are only read'; tests/integrations/test_eval_check.py:6-7 'the agent's artifacts are never modified'), so an unseeded script fails layer 2
repro: in an empty work dir W, solve.py is `from rand_engine import DataGenerator; DataGenerator({'age': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 0, 'max': 100}}}).size(10).get_df().to_csv('<W>/out.csv', index=False)` (unseeded, absolute path); run it once, then `PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<repo>/evals python -c "import sys,_check; from pathlib import Path; w=Path('.').resolve(); print(repr(_check.provenance(w, w/'solve.py', ['out.csv'], python=sys.executable)))"` in W prints None (exit 0), and the sha256 of out.csv changes (2278c9e6d663... before, bc84c7847071... after, on feature/0.8.2 fa397e2)
solution: provenance reads and hashes every delivered artifact (the not-delivered check, read_artifact, the column hashes) before the scratch copy and the re-run, then compares the re-run's record with those hashes: one path, evals/_check.py net 0; tests/integrations/test_eval_check.py pins the absolute-path rewrite and the symlink-loop artifact with their exact lines
symptom: an unseeded script that writes out.csv by its absolute path passes provenance (None), and the delivered out.csv is replaced by the re-run's output
title: provenance passes an unseeded script that writes its artifact by absolute path: the re-run overwrites the delivered artifact before provenance reads it

cause: REBUILD 7244f63 made unix_timestamps share _date_bounds without the DATE_DIRECTIVES check _dates applies and without a timezone rule, so a %z date_format parses timezone-aware bounds that epoch_seconds, which subtracts a naive epoch, cannot take; the validator accepted a spec neither engine generates (invariant 3)
context: _date_bounds (rand_engine/validators/method_specs.py) parses start and end under date_format and only compares them, so a %z format yields timezone-aware bounds that validate. Both engines convert bounds with epoch_seconds (rand_engine/core/_np_core.py:23), which subtracts a naive epoch, so every aware bound raises TypeError at generation: SparkGenerator.get_df raises it raw, and DataGenerator refuses it only through its construction-time probe. Found by the rc-4 Job 7 review (verdict 2026-11-07T232139Z, MEDIUM bug proposal) and reproduced by the main thread on feature/0.8.2 8d1914e.
expected: a spec that validates generates (specs/constitution.md:34, invariant 3: 'a validator accepts only methods and parameters the target engine runs'), so a timezone-aware bound is refused with a message naming the column
repro: with Java 17 and PYTHONPATH=<repo>: python -c "from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, functions as F; from rand_engine import SparkGenerator; from rand_engine.validators.common_validator import CommonValidator; spec = {'d': {'method': 'unix_timestamps', 'kwargs': {'start': '2020-01-01 +0000', 'end': '2021-01-01 +0000', 'date_format': '%Y-%m-%d %z'}}}; print(CommonValidator.validate_spark_spec(spec)); spark = SparkSession.builder.master('local[1]').getOrCreate(); SparkGenerator(spark, F, spec).size(3).get_df().collect()" prints [] and then raises TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes (feature/0.8.2 8d1914e)
solution: _date_bounds refuses a bound whose parse carries a tzinfo as it parses it, before any comparison: one rule for every caller, so the mixed aware/naive pair is refused too; tests/test_1_common_validator.py test_timezone_aware_date_bounds_are_refused_by_both_engines pins the full message on both validators
symptom: a unix_timestamps column with start '2020-01-01 +0000', end '2021-01-01 +0000' and date_format '%Y-%m-%d %z' passes CommonValidator.validate_spark_spec ([]), then SparkGenerator(spark, F, spec).size(3).get_df() raises TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
title: unix_timestamps validates timezone-aware start and end bounds that neither engine can generate: SparkGenerator.get_df raises TypeError

cause: b3cb8ef (0.8.2-rc3 J4.T2) wrote shutil.copytree(workdir, scratch), which follows every link, so a link in the work dir that is not an artifact and does not resolve (dangling, or a loop) stops the copy with shutil.Error before the re-run, and provenance raises instead of returning its line; efa19c9 rebuilt provenance's read order without touching that line
context: evals/_check.py provenance copies workdir into a scratch dir with shutil.copytree(workdir, scratch), which follows every link, so a link that is not an artifact and does not resolve stops the copy with shutil.Error before the re-run; provenance then raises instead of returning its line, and the task check exits with a traceback and no RESULT line. Reading the artifacts first fixed only the loop on an artifact path. Found by the hotfix review of eval-rerun-overwrites-delivered-artifact (verdict 2026-11-07T235126Z, MEDIUM bug proposal) and reproduced by the main thread on feature/0.8.2 ee6a839.
expected: provenance returns None or a line starting 'provenance', whatever else the work dir holds (tests/integrations/test_eval_check.py:4-7: 'provenance(workdir, script, artifacts, python=sys.executable, specs=None) -> None | str', 'A failure string starts "provenance"')
repro: in an empty dir with PYTHONPATH=<repo>: write solve.py = from rand_engine import DataGenerator; DataGenerator({'age': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 18, 'max': 80}}}, seed=1).size(10).get_df().to_csv('out.csv', index=False), run it, then ln -s missing.csv stale.csv; with PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<repo>/evals, python -c "import _check, sys; print(_check.provenance('.', 'solve.py', ['out.csv'], python=sys.executable))" raises shutil.Error naming stale.csv (feature/0.8.2 ee6a839); ln -s loop loop instead raises shutil.Error: Too many levels of symbolic links
solution: the scratch copy copies only what resolves: copytree's ignore callable drops each name whose path in its own directory does not exist, and valid links are still followed as before, so nothing in the copy points outside it (no symlinks=True, which without rc-4's R8 would let the cleanup or the re-run reach outside the copy); tests/integrations/test_eval_check.py pins a dangling link and a self-loop that are not artifacts
symptom: a seeded script whose work dir also holds stale.csv -> missing.csv (or loop -> loop) makes provenance raise shutil.Error ([Errno 2] No such file or directory, or [Errno 40] Too many levels of symbolic links) instead of returning None
title: provenance raises shutil.Error instead of grading when the work dir holds a dangling or looping symlink that is not an artifact

cause: c8b7398 (0.8.2-rc3 J4.T2) made the recording shim read RAND_EVAL_RECORD at exit, and provenance's re-run env hands the shim (first on PYTHONPATH) and RAND_EVAL_RECORD to every Python process the script starts; each loads the shim as sitecustomize and its atexit dump rewrites the one record file, so the last process to exit wins: Spark's pyspark/daemon.py outlives a driver that does not call spark.stop() and writes an empty record over the script's
context: provenance's re-run env puts the shim dir first on PYTHONPATH and sets RAND_EVAL_RECORD (evals/_check.py:174-176). Every Python process the script starts inherits both, loads the shim as sitecustomize, and its atexit dump (evals/_check.py:98-104) rewrites the one record file, so the last process to exit wins. subprocess.run(capture_output=True) waits for every holder of the pipes, so the overwrite lands before provenance reads the record. SparkGenerator's pk/fk path starts pyspark/daemon.py, which outlives the driver when the script does not call spark.stop(). That is why the repro of eval-spark-multipart-dir-fails-provenance stays red after its value_hash fix. Found by the hotfix review of that bug (verdict 2026-11-11T015507Z, a MEDIUM bug proposal) and reproduced by the main thread on feature/0.8.2 0e29754, 3/3, without Spark.
expected: a seeded script whose artifact rand_engine generated passes provenance whatever child processes it starts (evals/tasks/spark-generator/tests/check.py:4: 'Layer 2: make.py re-runs through rand_engine's SparkGenerator and reproduces both columns'; evals/tasks/spark-generator/instruction.md asks for no spark.stop())
repro: in an empty dir with PYTHONPATH=<repo>: write solve.py = import subprocess, sys; from rand_engine import DataGenerator; DataGenerator({'age': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 18, 'max': 80}}}, seed=1).size(10).get_df().to_csv('out.csv', index=False); subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-c', 'import time; time.sleep(2)']) and run it; then with PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<repo>/evals, python -c "import _check, sys; print(_check.provenance('.', 'solve.py', ['out.csv'], python=sys.executable))" prints "provenance: column 'age' of out.csv matches no frame rand_engine generated" (3/3 on feature/0.8.2 0e29754); without the Popen line it prints None. With Spark: the repro of eval-spark-multipart-dir-fails-provenance (no spark.stop()) fails the same way at its fix bc66cd8 and passes with spark.stop() added
solution: the record belongs to the process that runs the script: the shim takes RAND_EVAL_RECORD out of the environment when it loads, so no child inherits it, and a process without it records nothing; tests/integrations/test_eval_check.py pins a seeded script that leaves a child Python process running, which passes provenance. The contract lines, verbatim: evals/_check.py:150 'None when every artifact column equals a column the script generated through rand_engine on a re-run, else a "provenance: ..." line.' and evals/tasks/spark-generator/tests/check.py:4 'Layer 2: `make.py` re-runs through rand_engine's SparkGenerator and reproduces both columns.'
symptom: a seeded script that leaves a child Python process running fails provenance with 'column ... matches no frame rand_engine generated'; the same script without the child passes
title: provenance fails a seeded script whose re-run leaves a child Python process running (Spark's worker daemon among them): the child inherits the recording shim and RAND_EVAL_RECORD, and its exit dump overwrites the script's record with an empty one

context: provenance copies workdir into a scratch dir with shutil.copytree, which follows every link that resolves (evals/_check.py:173). A directory link to '.' or to an ancestor is copied as a real directory about 40 levels deep, until the path hits ELOOP; two such links make the copy branch at every level, so it grows exponentially and provenance returns neither None nor a 'provenance' line. Found by the hotfix review of eval-provenance-crashes-on-stray-link (verdict 2026-11-11T021018Z, a pre-existing finding) and reproduced by the main thread on feature/0.8.2 a9bf84d.
expected: provenance returns None or a line starting 'provenance', whatever links the work dir holds (tests/integrations/test_eval_check.py:5: 'provenance(workdir, script, artifacts, python=sys.executable, specs=None) -> None | str', :8: 'A failure string starts "provenance"')
repro: in an empty dir with PYTHONPATH=<repo>: write solve.py = from rand_engine import DataGenerator; DataGenerator({'age': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 18, 'max': 80}}}, seed=1).size(10).get_df().to_csv('out.csv', index=False), run it, then ln -s . a; ln -s . b; with PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<repo>/evals, timeout 15 python -c "import _check, sys; print(_check.provenance('.', 'solve.py', ['out.csv'], python=sys.executable))" exits 124 with nothing printed while the scratch copy under TMPDIR grows (154M at 15 s, feature/0.8.2 a9bf84d); without b it prints None
solution: 240a98f (0.8.2-rc4 J4.T4) copies with shutil.copytree(workdir, scratch, symlinks=True), so links stay links and the copy holds only the work dir's own entries, and refuses an artifact that resolves outside the copy; 1f47ff8 pins two links to '.' passing provenance (without symlinks=True the case hangs: exit 124 at 20 s)
symptom: a seeded script whose work dir also holds a -> . and b -> . makes provenance run until killed (no return after 15 s, 154 MB of scratch copy; the review measured 1.1 GB at 40 s); with only a -> . it returns None in 3 s
title: provenance never returns when the work dir holds two directory links to an ancestor: the scratch copy follows them and grows without bound

cause: c8b7398 (0.8.2-rc3 J4.T2) made the recording shim dump its frames to RAND_EVAL_RECORD at exit; the fix of eval-shim-record-overwritten-by-child-process took the variable out of the environment when the shim loads, which stops an exec'd child but not a forked one: fork copies the module global RECORD and the atexit dump, so a forked child that leaves through the interpreter dumps its own copy of the frames over the record
context: The recording shim takes RAND_EVAL_RECORD out of the environment when it loads (evals/_check.py:34), so an exec'd child records nothing. os.fork() copies the module global RECORD and the atexit dump (evals/_check.py:99-107), so a forked child that leaves through the interpreter (sys.exit or the end of its code) dumps its own copy of the frames over the record. multiprocessing and pyspark daemon children leave through os._exit and are not affected; Windows has no fork. Found by the hotfix review of eval-shim-record-overwritten-by-child-process (verdict 2026-11-11T022849Z, a MEDIUM bug proposal), reproduced by the main thread at 806fa2c 3/3 and by the review at a9bf84d.
expected: a seeded script whose artifact rand_engine generated passes provenance whatever child processes it starts (the expected of eval-shim-record-overwritten-by-child-process; evals/_check.py:150: 'None when every artifact column equals a column the script generated through rand_engine on a re-run')
repro: in an empty dir with PYTHONPATH=<repo>: write solve.py = import os, sys, time; from rand_engine import DataGenerator; then if os.fork() == 0: time.sleep(1); sys.exit(0); then DataGenerator({'age': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 18, 'max': 80}}}, seed=1).size(10).get_df().to_csv('out.csv', index=False); run it; then with PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<repo>/evals, python -c "import _check, sys; print(_check.provenance('.', 'solve.py', ['out.csv'], python=sys.executable))" prints "provenance: column 'age' of out.csv matches no frame rand_engine generated" (3/3, exit 0, at 806fa2c)
solution: the record belongs to the process that loaded the shim with RAND_EVAL_RECORD set: the shim reads the variable and its own pid when it loads (evals/_check.py:34: RECORD, OWNER = os.environ.pop("RAND_EVAL_RECORD", None), os.getpid()), and dump returns unless that process exits (:101), so an exec'd child (no variable) and a forked child (another pid) record nothing; tests/integrations/test_eval_check.py:375 pins a forked child that calls sys.exit(0), skipped where os.fork does not exist; the record's repro prints None 3 of 3 at this lane's head
symptom: a seeded script that forks a child which sleeps 1 s and calls sys.exit(0) fails provenance with: column 'age' of out.csv matches no frame rand_engine generated; the same script without the fork passes
title: provenance fails a seeded script that forks a child which outlives it and exits through the interpreter: the child keeps the shim's record path, and its exit dump overwrites the script's record

cause: 678f6bf (T-070-13) judged each benchmark row by statistics.median of its RUNS=3 samples, and 33ac8a7 (T-070-18) kept that median in the interleaved run(). Runner noise only adds time, so two inflated samples of three moved a 4-11 ms row's median past 1.3x with no code change (run 42954318116: distincts at 1M 1.40 while 10M gave 0.94; a local A/B gives 0.95-0.99)
context: run() judges each A/B row by statistics.median of RUNS=3 interleaved samples per side (benchmarks/speed.py:307,309; specs/memory/product/quality/benchmarks.md:23 'compares their medians') against LIMIT 1.3 (:64). At 1M rows several rows take 4-11 ms (run 42954318116: integers 4.1 ms, distincts 8.1 ms, booleans 11.5 ms), so a shared runner that adds a few ms to two of the three samples on one side moves the median past 1.3x with no code change; the interleaving evens out drift across the run, not a burst inside one row. The gate runs on every pull request to the principal and integration branches (.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml:4-5); a rerun is the only workaround and nothing documents it.
expected: A row fails only when it is slower than 1.3 times its base: specs/memory/product/quality/benchmarks.md:31 'Any comparable method or sink row slower than 1.3 times its base fails the job'; specs/memory/product/index.md:71 'CI enforces same-runner rand-engine regression limits'; benchmarks/speed.py:274 'exit ... 1 over LIMIT'. A distincts row measuring 0.95-0.99 of its base passes.
repro: gh run view 42954318116 --log-failed | grep 'over 1.3x' prints over 1.3x base: [('distincts', 1000000)] (the Speed benchmark step exits 1); an interleaved A/B of DataGenerator({'c': {'method': 'distincts', 'kwargs': {'distincts': ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']}}}, seed=42).size(1000000).get_df(), 48 samples per side, git archive 0.8.1 against git archive b9603bd, gives a median head/base of 0.953.
solution: cd775e9 REBUILDs run()'s per-row statistic as min() of each side's samples, the timeit guidance: noise only adds time, so the ratio crosses LIMIT only when every head sample is slow, as in a real regression. RUNS, LIMIT, the sizes and the interleaving are unchanged. ecb5f00 pins a row with one base-speed head sample passing and a uniformly slow head failing
symptom: Benchmarks run 42954318116 (wt/0.8.2/rc-4/wt-rc at b9603bd, base tag 0.8.1 at 46ce1b1) exited 1 with over 1.3x base: [('distincts', 1000000)], base 0.008 s and head 0.011 s (1.40), while distincts at 10M gave 0.94 in the same run. An interleaved local A/B of the same row, 48 get_df samples per side against git archive 0.8.1, gives head/base 0.953 for git archive b9603bd and 0.990 for the rc-4 wt-rc tree, whose rand_engine/ is b9603bd's.
title: The speed benchmark gate fails a row whose code did not slow down: the median of three samples reads millisecond runner noise as a regression over 1.3x
